name: 2024 Red Sea Maritime Chokepoint & Conflict Crisis
affected_country: Red Sea / Bab el-Mandeb / European Ports
severity_rationale: Drone and anti-ship missile attacks on commercial vessels near Bab el-Mandeb forced major container liners (Maersk, MSC, Hapag-Lloyd) to divert around the Cape of Good Hope, adding 10 to 14 sailing days and 400% container spot freight increases between Asia and Europe. Combines armed geopolitical conflict with severe logistics container delays.
source_org: UNCTAD (United Nations Trade & Development) / Reuters / IMF PortWatch
notes_on_facts: UNCTAD reported an 82% year-over-year decline in Suez Canal container ship transits by mid-January 2024. Represents multi-signal compounding of security conflict and maritime transit disruption.

events.headline: Commercial container carriers suspend Red Sea voyages following missile strikes on merchant ships
events.summary: Armed attacks on commercial shipping vessels in the Bab el-Mandeb Strait prompt leading ocean container carriers to halt Red Sea transit due to direct security risks.

events.headline: Cape of Good Hope container rerouting adds 12 days transit and triggers acute port arrival delays
events.summary: Ocean container lines routing vessels around Africa report transit extensions of 10 to 14 days, creating equipment shortages and vessel arrival clustering at North European terminals.
